Maya: quick heads-up — sprint got squeezed. We need to decide what's in alpha for the Optimize Toolkit: batching, caching, quant recs, eval-triggered alerts. Customer asks (Acme + Slate) pressing. Thoughts?

Liam: if we only pick two, my vote is batching + eval-alerts. Quant recs are heavier infra + model-op work.

Sophia: +1 to batching + eval alerts. Quant recommendations need per-model profiling and a safe fallback path — risky for alpha.

Alex: FYI, customer asks: Acme wants per-prompt eval hooks + immediate alerts on regressions. Slate is asking for explicit quant guidance and a simple config wizard.

Jen: infra note — eval-triggered alerts need storage for reference prompt sets + eval results. We can do a lightweight approach: sample-based evals every 6h and keep a rolling window. Storage impact should be small.

Maya: proposed tradeoff: alpha = batching + eval-alerts (minimal storage + simple thresholds); beta = caching + quant recs. Anyone opposed?

Liam: agree. For batching we should expose target latency SLO and a batch window. Proposed fields: `batch_window_ms`, `target_p99_ms`. Example default: `batch_window_ms=15`.

Sophia: for eval alerts propose thresholds like `concordance_drop_pct=5` or `wer_increase_pct=3`. Also need a rollup metric to track false positives so customers can tune sensitivity.

Alex: customers will accept an opt-in alpha: alerts go to ops channel + customer webhook. They want the webhook payload to include the failing prompt IDs and a small diff.

Maya: acceptance criteria for alpha (draft): 1) batching enabled in SDK with documented knobs; 2) eval-alert pipeline that runs on sample set; 3) alerting to ops channel + webhook; 4) sample prompt set + docs + runbook; 5) measured cost delta < 15% in our CI perf harness. Any blockers?

Jen: blocker — we need a tiny persistence schema for reference evals and a short retention policy. I'll carve out an index in infra and prototype storage + TTL. ETA ~2 weeks.

Liam: implementation note: continuous batching will improve throughput but we need to ensure KV cache invalidation semantics remain stable when requests are batched. I'll add unit tests for key eviction scenarios.

Maya: decision: locking alpha scope to batching + eval-alerts. Caching and quant recs go to backlog as beta items with EPICs. I'll update roadmap doc + ping sales to reset expectations.

deploy-bot: Maya pinned a message in #product :pushpin:

Alex: quick follow-up — I'll draft the customer-facing alpha summary and list the opt-in steps for Acme/Slate.

Sophia: I'll prepare a tiny eval harness and the default thresholds for the sample set — will share before EOD Friday.

Maya: thanks all. I'll post the acceptance checklist and open the kickoff ticket after lunch. :+1:
